One of the problems with implementing a Zombie mode is figuring out what kind of spawning mode to use. Do you use team spawns, or individual spawns? How will one implement the placement of zombie spawns? How do you account for 16 players or having more than 8 zombies concurrently spawned when using team spawns? What settings are planned to be implemented? How do you plan to supply players throughout the round?

I personally would tackle these questions with the following answers. Team spawns for PvE/Co-Op Zombie Hell, individual spawns for PvP Zombie Infection. Use the opposing team's spawns for Zombie Hell, Individual spawns for Zombie Infection, random player gets selected to be zombie after a certain number of seconds. Have players/zombies either spawn on top of each other or one after another as soon as a spawn area is free. title: A basic guide to Brick Force!

posts.h:
What is Brick Force?

Brick Force is the worlds first cross platform sandbox shooter which launched for closed beta on the 28th Febrary. The game has been noted as one of the best sandbox games at the moment.

How do i play?

1. Register at the official Brick-Force homepage.

2. Get a beta key from a giveaway.

3. Activate the key at the website.

4. You will get a link to download the game. (Note: You may need to wait a few weeks for this email)

5. Wait for your account to be unlocked (All accounts are now unlocked!)

6. Log in and you can play!

The Different game mode:

1. The ‘sandbox’ mode, in which players use simple building blocks to construct complex environments, can be played on social networks and mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets. With a range of different brick styles to choose from, combined with the possibility to place key interactive elements such as turrets or bomb sites, players will find themselves challenged in numerous creative ways.

Players will find themselves stepping into the shoes of both map builder and game designer. They will have the opportunity to dazzle their team mates with creativity, and the most talented map designers will be rewarded handsomely for their efforts.

2. The ‘shooter’ mode is an action orientated platform with a range of different game types which will be familiar to fans of team-based shooters. Classic modes such as Team and Solo Deathmatch, Capture the Flag and Blast Mode are all in place.

Players can choose from a wide variety of different guns, weapons and armor with different stats and functions.

Challenges deployed by the map creators must be overcome using teamwork, skill and reactions to defeat opposing teams. Social features such as a clan system have been integrated, allowing gamers to team up with their friends and compete for fame and glory.

I saw there wasn't currently a big fix/suggestion thread, so I figured I'd make one, and throw in all the things that I found. I sorted them into three categories: fixes that need to be implemented (bugs), fixes that should be implemented (balance and such), suggestions that should probably be in the game, and suggestions I think would be cool in the game. The list is a bit long, but only because I really would love to see this game be amazing. ;D

Need to be fixed:
  1. Invincible dead body glitch? (Still alive, but look like a dead body and can't be killed, but can still kill)
  2. Going down slopes makes you fall periodically rather than go smoothly down
  3. You are able to move in the air slightly if you walk off of something, but not if you jump (Should be changed to move in the air no matter what)
  4. Game should be able to be started as soon as an even (or difference of one) number of people are ready on each team, not when everyone is ready
  5. Snipers deal too much damage
  6. I've heard headshots are based on %LCK and not actual hitboxes or something similar? Luck should not affect headshots; there should just be a head hitbox and the game should count it as a headshot if it is a headshot.
  7. When you fire a gun in any gamemode or pick up the neutral flag in CTF, your spawn protection should disappear (as you obviously no longer need it)
  8. No waiting for people to load before you can move in Team Battle
  9. No waiting for people to load *ever* while midgame
  10. The heartbeat sound when low on health only needs to play once or twice, not infinitely. This is not Pokémon.
  11. Hats make you taller (For example, make you able to be seen behind 2blockhigh barricades)
  12. 'The amount that hats make you taller' does not actually add a hitbox (To solve this AND the previous problem, make hats fit snugly to your head)
  13. Ladders are near impossible to climb up if you start your ascent up the ladder by walking straight into it. Somehow, it doesn't let you come close enough to the ladder, so when you get to the top, you just fall down. Unless, however, you can make to "grab" back onto the ladder. In this case you'll be closer to the ladder, and able to dismount it correctly at the top.
    tl;dr: Ladders are broken
  14. Dead bodies [still have a hitbox and still show names when moused over] for a few seconds after death
  15. Falling down a 1x1 hole is *extremely* difficult
  16. Running into people occasionally makes you walk on top of them, even if you're not jumping
  17. Running sound plays even while not moving (i.e. Running into a wall or a corner)
  18. If people join a Blast round in progress, they will show up as alive (white name) in the Tab menu, even though they are dead
  19. You can still switch to the grenade, even if you don't have a grenade
  20. 'Next round is about to begin' covers up the top person on Blue's score in Blast
  21. "Allow players to join midgame" option covers the lobby chat
  22. Your ping always shows as '0', even if you're not the host
  23. Players will sound like they're next to you, even if they're 100 blocks above you. (Z axis not taken into effect when calculating sound volume)
  24. When you look at someone's Player Info, the XP bar is actually your XP
  25. Spamming Shift (The walk key) spams footstep noises faster than usual
  26. If you switch weapons right before death, the view model of the weapon will still be in your hands
  27. When typing while dead in Blast, spacebar still changes what player you're viewing
  28. If you are the host of the game and you press ESC while someone is loading, you can't leave the Kick menu. You have to wait until everyone loads.


Should be fixed:
  1. If you enter a second before your team loses, it still goes as a loss in your stats [More of an egotistical thing here, but it still bothers me D:]
  2. Having to buy bricks *needs* to be taken away. Will probably do separate post on this, as it is very detrimental to the game.
  3. Rating system is flawed. (Will do another post on this, too)
  4. You only get 100 points for bombing the bombsite. Unsure on defusal, but both should be around 300.
  5. There is too much of an XP/Point penalty for losing. People with far better scores are getting far less points than others.
  6. Bomb timer should be 45ish seconds rather than the current 30. It takes 7ish to defuse, leaving you 23 seconds to get to the bombsite, kill everyone, and find the bomb.
  7. You slow down while jumping (Doesn't feel natural)
  8. HMGs do way too much damage (80ish), but are too inaccurate, thus their uses are very limited

Should be implemented:
  1. After death stats showing damage dealt to each person
  2. Warmup round while waiting for people to load in Blast
  3. Flying in Map Edit mode
  4. Some sort of box tool in Map Edit mode (Selecting a 'box' of cubes to change, rather than 1 at a time)
  5. The ability to click and hold the left click and right click features in Map Edit to repeatedly place or remove blocks.
  6. Some way to get ammo midlife (Probably by picking it up off of dead bodies)
  7. 'Q' should default to either your pistol or your wrench, rather than doing nothing before your first weapon switch
  8. Some way to crouch
  9. Team chat
  10. Colorcoded chat (Blue members are blue, red members are red, team chat is green, all chat is white, clan chat is purple, etc.)
  11. On loading screen: Map picture and name of the map
  12. The ability to change game type without having to remake the lobby.


Would like to see implemented:
  1. Swimming and/or Water
  2. Some sort of unbreakable glass block
  3. Classic CTF mode (Take enemies' flag back to your flag stand)
  4. VoIP

There's also a bug ran into where, if you are the host of the game and you press ESC while someone is loading, you can't leave the Kick menu. You have to wait until everyone loads.

Also, bullet hits seem to register quite slowly, allowing people to kill each other at the same time, for someone to kill while being out of sight, dying several seconds after being fired at, etc. Not sure if it's just server lag or a bug.

title: What sort of maps would you like to play in the future?

posts.h:
This thread is for sharing design and visual ideas for map-edits that you would like to see realized, and as a way to inspire map editors looking for ideas on what to build next. If you want an export of a certain map from a certain other game, then you have to state why it's a good idea.

Me, personally, I would like to see some gothic castles, gothic castles are awesome for their atmosphere and their beautiful symmetry, making balancing for team battle modes very easy. Something like what you would see in the Castlevania games. Various dungeons from the 2-D Zelda Games are fairly good fodder for maze-like maps with jumping puzzles. I would also be very happy to see a recreation of the Parthenon temple complex or a part of the city of Luxor or Karnak. Scaled down Wolfenstein maps are good for maze type action that is cheap to register, due to the low amount of special bricks needed. A large multi-level underground office complex that looks like a zombie outbreak has ravaged it is also something I would love to see. I also REALLY want to see a remake of Dusty with extra paths areas, and with the problem of going out of the level taken care of. Floating islands with bridges made of wood connecting them is a map idea I haven't seen created yet.

For a more explained detail on closed and open beta, there are 3 steps to follow when playing a game:

Closed Beta: It is the time when the developers are currently making the items in-game, to resolve most of the bugs and to get player's feedback. The game may be for public or private depending on how developers wanted. Before open beta, they can opt for allowing players to retain or delete their player's accounts.

Open Beta: It is the time when the public gets to play the game. They will try to get as much as player feedback as possible. All basic mechanics and items are release during this time.

Fully released game: It is the time after the open beta, when the developers will release new items, updates and maintenance every month.

title: FreeToPlay is limiting this games potential...

Anyone else feel this way?

I really don't want to rent weapons/items. Then I will be annoyed if I suddenly have a whole week occupied by work/life. This happens, and there is no way around it!

I would gladly pay a full retail price of something like $60! Then I could play the game whenever I wanted to without being limited by items that I couldn't access...

Servers wouldn't be a problem as these would be hosted by fans/clans/communities! Just like they already are in countless other games! Minecroft, Counter-Stroke, Call of Dope etc.

And let's not forget mods! The fans setting the boundaries of the game!

A full retail game could feature the whole package meaning map editor, multiplayer and perhaps a few singleplayer game modes.

And this would probably make a lot of you excited: the map editor could be distributed freely using Bittorrent or something to make the distribution cost nothing. This would allow any creative mind to jump into the editor and create something for the paying customers. No stupid paying to use decorative blocks or paying to let others play your map. And just like current plans, the map editor would also be sold on mobile devices for a few bucks.

*sigh* I'll go to a corner and cry now... thanks for reading.

THIS THREAD IS HEAVILY UNDER CONSTRUCTION

Introduction

Please take the time to read through our rules. Ok first things first, this thread is purely for clans who would like to play under these rules for clanwars, that means you don't have to play under them. All the clans who would like to play under these rules will be listed in this thread. If this is going to be a succes and many clans and people support me, i will also host some tournaments with prizes etc. And ofcourse official ladders.

Match rules

All matches are played using the Max Rounds 9 scoring system.
A match is played over either one or two maps, if they are playing only one map the challengers can choose the map, when playing on two maps each clan picks their own map. Challengers may choose first. (It's possible to play twice at the same map)
Each clan will play one time as Attackers (The ones that must plant the bomb) and one time as Defenders. (The ones that has to disarm the bomb if armed)
There is a limit of one sniper per team, using more than one sniper in a team may result in a forfeit loss.
Only five on five matches are allowed. All matches that are played with a different equal/unequal teamsize (Two on two, three on three, two on three, etc) will be cancelled.

Miscellaneous rules

Not knowing the rules is never a valid excuse for not following them.
If all the players on one team drops because of technical error, the other team should wait at least 5 minutes before leaving the server.
If a player drops because of a technical error you must pause the match at the end of the round (never during a round). The maximum time you can pause is 10 minutes, which is enough time to reboot and reconnect. Unpausing the match before the time is up without the missing player and without the agreement of the opponent will result in withdrawing 2 roundwins from the abusing team and giving them to the opponent. If one team has paused the match for a total of more than 10 minutes, the other team may either demand that the match continues without waiting for the missing players or that the match is cancelled.
Substituting players is allowed at any time during a match, but you'll have to convince your opponent to pause the match if you want to do it in the middle of a round.
If one team willingly leaves the room before the match is finished, the clan that stayed are awarded the remaining rounds. (They win the match)

Maplist

These are the only maps we support, if you want to add your map to the list send Baek a private message. (In game or on the forums doesn't really matter)

mp_dusty
mp_aztec

Cheating & Abuse

Cheating

If a player cheats, (Aimbot, Wallhack, Etc) the player will get blacklisted and kicked out of the clan, if not kicked out of the clan the whole clan will be blacklisted.
If a player uses a glitch, (Example: Climbing on top of dusty) the opposing clan will win the match be a forfeit. When a player cheats, (Aimbot, Wallhack, Etc) in a public lobby the player will be blacklisted and kicked out of the clan, if not kicked out of the clan the whole will be blacklisted.
Producing/distributing cheats, (Aimbot, Wallhack, Etc) is strictly forbidden and once again you will get blacklisted and kicked out of the clan, if not kicked out of the clan the whole clan will be blacklisted

Abuse

Don't use racism in any kind
Don't harass anyone
Bothering people with off-topic advertising in other words, uninteresting advertisements (Example: Use my referral id to sign up so I make money or get points) Of course you are allowed to advertise clanpages and player pages.

Don't copy anything without permission ~ Baek

Map Size: 1F,50x50
Server: EU
Modes: TDM, Survival, Blast, CTF
Finished: 2012.3.13
Clan: .HUNGARY.

Description (info):

When we built our new map, the main point was to make a playable well designed one. Our first try was a huge, fancy (100x100) map which cost more then 70.000 but it was still empty, and loading a lot at the begginings. It was boring even with 16 players (just like a maze). So we decided to build a smaller, less flashy but a quicker and enjoyable map (we hope we did it)! :)

It's a mirror map so the chance is equal for both teams/players. All modes are allowed (CTF,blast,survival or team deathmatch) All class has a spot on the map to prevail, but you need a strategy first.

661663664665666

Advantages:

-If you get baseraped (on TDM), then you have the oportunity to choose 2 more ways from your spawnspot. (tunnel system)
-We built our buildings quite low so you won't suffer a huge HP loss when you jump or fall down.
-You can easily walk through roof to roof because the objects are close to each other.
-There are a lot of destroyable transparent glasses so you can trick your enemy.
-The 2 side has a different colour (red/blue, still the tunnel has) so you can easily realize where you are.

Tips:

-You can fall down at the center point, so be careful:)
-If you play survival mode, then you should prefer machineguns, and NEVER stop. :)
-If you play CTF mode, then the easiest way to reach the flag, if you shoot out the windows at the begginings and then use the ladders at the side of the buildings. To score a goal, you should take the flag to the enemies' tower.

Description: An abandoned factory that once beat the odds and became the biggest of its kind. Now has become a war zone for territorial control.

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vrPE17eVpF8&feature=youtu.beMap name: Smee Tower

This map is based off the extremely popular mini game map called mg_smeetower on Counter-Strike:Source.

Plot: The BLU Brickforce team is trying to eliminate ALL RED Brickforce members inside the tower
AKA The Counter-Terrorists are trying to take out all Terrorists inside the tower.

Red has spawnpoints on the second floor of the building,and on the roof of it.
Blu has spawnpoints at the bottom of the building on the 1st floor, in a helicopter, and behind a small Minigun position.

I have carefully thought this out and this map and balanced out all sides of the map so not one team gets all the advantages and the other doesn't.

There are ladders on both side of buildings that lead to the top of the tower.These ladders lead to the top of the tower where RED Snipers could be hiding. There are also some cover near the ladders so people can take cover if they are opened fire on when they try to get to the top by ladder. The cover for the right ladders is a pool where BLU can hide behind in case they got fired on by RED guarding the ladders. The cover for the left ladders is a tiny Outhouse that BLU members can hide beside if they get opened fire on by the RED.

There is a staircase leading directly from the 1st floor to the 2nd floor but is very narrow and quite long and any charging foe can be easily eliminated by a wrench in the narrow staircase.

There is a ladder inside the 1st floor that leads directly into RED Spawnpoint(2nd Floor) so it won't be quite easy to get to the top.

There is a small stationary minigun in front of the tower where BLU spawns behind. It can provide covering fire for BLU members coming out of the helicopter when they spawn. However the Minigun has only a few sandbags and can be easily taken out by a pistol shot from the top of the tower.

There is 2 sets of outer layers outside the building accessible by the ladders. These are for the RED opening fire on the Minigun/ Trying to stop BLU members from getting to the ladders/ or just plain shooting there.

There is breakable windows everywhere so there is cover but not too much cover inside the building. The breakable windows serves as a limited protection against bullets and places to fire from if getting sieged on by the Minigun.

At first I ran into a problem of a bug where a red flag was placed invisibly somewhere and that prevented me from finishing my map. I had to wait about a week and reported my bug to the Brickforce Blog and they got it fixed (I THINK). I had 3 helpers but I forgot their names but they placed their initials on the map on the ground ^^.
The map took me about 3-4 hours to finish it and about 10,000 Brick Credits to register it. It supports all 4 gamemodes and is my second map. I have personally tested it and it is CRAZY FUN. I set my game up and 1 minute later the entire room was full! I got compliments on how my map was good (Not boasting/Exaggerating).

Thanks for waiting ^^, and my map is made in the American Server

What is a stress test?

The stress test is a designated testing period in which we aim to put maximum pressure on the game servers by allowing every registered user access to Brick-Force. The goal is to test the capabilities of our hardware.

Who can participate in the stress test?

Every user who has registered a game account (with a Nickname and Password) can take part in the stress test, regardless of whether or not you have a beta key or an unlocked account.


When will the testing take place?

During the following designated testing periods:

  • Start: Thursday 22nd March, 16:00 CET / 11:00 EDT / 8:00 PDT
  • End: Friday 23rd March, 16:00 CET / 11:00 EDT / 8:00 PDT

  • Start: Tuesday 27th March, 16:00 CET / 11:00 EDT / 8:00 PDT
  • End: Wednesday 28th March, 16:00 CET / 11:00 EDT / 8:00 PDT

  • Start: Saturday 31st March, 16:00 CET / 11:00 EDT / 8:00 PDT
  • End: Tuesday 3rd April, 16:00 CET / 11:00 EDT / 8:00 PDT


What’s the purpose of the stress test?

The goal is to analyze the performance of our servers to ensure that we have greater stability and performance when the open beta is launched.

I can’t log in because the login server is down/the patch server is not responding/I can’t click on the “Start” button.

During the stress test you might well experience problems such as connection issues, server shutdowns or other irregularities. This is all part of the experience – we need to experiment and push our servers to the limit to help us launch a smooth and stable open beta.

What will happen once the stress test has ended?

After the stress test phase has been finished, we will limit access to the Brick-Force servers again. If your account has already been unlocked, you will be able to continue to play Brick-Force during the closed beta.

title: HEADSHOTS - Fix it or remove it.

posts.h:
Ive played for about 2 weeks now and I am pretty advanced rank with an average 73% KDR.

Headshots are random. And involving luck is a FPS game like this is no good. Good players dont want to be down on the same level as a noob. Cus both of them have the same change to 1 shot the other. And theres nothing more frustrating than to get 1 shot by a noob with a 35% KDR. It should be only skills involved.
What I propose is:
-Let the player be able to aim down his sight. This will really set a wall between the good and bad players.
or
-Allow HS to be only appliable when the player's health is under 50. That way if a good player is low on health, he will play more careful knowing he will get 1 shot. Therefor is he dies it will be hes only responsibility cus he knew he would be killed by 1 bullet.
or
-Get rid of headshots and increase weapon damage.

This is perfect time to take action to fix this issue. And you will get a more large variety play styles. Clans will also be way more competitive and not just the average clans playing agains in friendly matches.. there could be opportunities for tournaments and prices (profesionnal players like that stuff).

The player's stats will really represent what he is worth, either if he is good or less good. I speak for all the good players out there that want a balanced game. Because a non-balanced game is a bad game. Hope you guys will consider this issue.

Thanks for your time DDDD This game is awesome besides that. (Why you think Im still playing?)

Originally Posted by KDraconis
I'm pretty sure it's headshots are random AFTER a bullet hits you in the face. Once you hit someone in the head, the game calculates how much Luck that player has, and then does a roll on whether or not you succeed at a headshot or just deal basic damage.

In that way, Luck is basically the quality of your head protection; a good helmet can deflect one or two bullets.

What I'm worried about is that high-tier items will give enough Luck to make veteran players untouchable to new players.
Also, about spray... A lot of players would argue that controlling your weapon's spray is a part of skill. E.g. anyone who has played Counter-Strike.

Oh, and the game only screams "Headshot!" if you kill someone with a headshot. You still deal extra damage when you hit the head no matter what, at least from what I've tested. And considering the maximum Luck you can get with the items currently in the shop is around 4%... Only one out of twenty-five bullets won't kill your target. I have maximum Luck and it barely ever procs on me.

I think you're taking this with the mindset that because it's hipfire, it's like CoD hipfire, and so it sprays and is not accurate. If you actually control your shots, the first bullet will pretty much always go straight. The bullets only spray if you, yourself are spraying.

title: Teaming up - Map Design. Read for info.

posts.h:
AN UPDATE!

So far so good on the 2 Fort Map. Please read below! Here are a few pictures of what I've been working on!



Greetings friends!

My name is Moya. I became interested in Brick-Force sometime in January, and gathered as much as I could to see what was possible. And to much avail, I've become addicted with such a simplistic building scheme. My main focus will be mapping, as I tend to indulge myself with creation. In particular, I'll be working on CTF maps, because I enjoy more objective-based teamwork when it comes to FPS gaming.

The map I am currently re-creating for Brick-Force is known as 2 Fort. Many of you have probably heard of or seen this map in fortress games and mods such as Team Fortress 2, Fortress Forever, Team Fortress Classic, Quake Fortress, ETF, etc etc.

At the moment, the model is near half way finished. Once I finish the model full 100%, I'll be seeking more players to join me in "re-texturing" the model. At the moment, I use 1 block to get the model done quicker. Then go back and actually replace the blocks with actual blocks that make the map more team distinguishable (Red Base / Blue Base). This is where I will need the help of other players. Here is a tiny breakdown of my goals using the 100x100 map size:

1) Make 2 fort - 100%

2) Replace blocks with team based distinguishable blocks - 0%

3) Remove the complete 100x100 map floor - 0% ( This doesn't include the blocks that are originally apart of the floor blocks.)

This map is not for the contest that is being held currently, because I dont feel the need to rush with my actual life being more important. This is just more of a hobby, and something I can provide to other players because I believe there won't be much going on for the CTF map making.

Any feedback is welcome on this. I encourage those willing to help to inform me as soon as possible. I'll be working on this heavily over the weekend. Thank you for reading, and hope to see some replies soon

~Moya

title: Things I've noticed and my Suggestions towards them

posts.h:
I'm not going to list these in any particular order. These are my personal opinions, feel free to agree, disagree or tare them apart.

*•Guns are very inaccurate. When I play I either pick Sniper because I get to actually aim at people, or if the map is close corridors I pick the machine gun with 75 ammo and spray while walking around corners. I would really like to see either (A) Guns made far more accurate (B) Put aiming down the sights in to increase accuracy so people can aim rather than spraying and praying. On a side note, I'd like to see the mounted guns have more accuracy. Now you just aim towards someone and hope for the best.

I've seen a lot of hate towards sniper rifles, but I think some of this hate besides the one-shot capabilities of the sniper are the result of them being able to aim you down from much further away than a non sniper can.

*•In regards to accuracy, random head shots. I know the bullet hit you in the head, but when most fights are determined by who started spraying at the other one first it is annoying to see the almost random head shots appear. I get them too, you don't even have to be aiming at the head to get one. I've even seen them on the mounted vulcan cannons and you can't tell me someone is actually aiming that perfectly at someones head to shoot them. I'm not sure what can be done with regards to this, or if anything can be, but with the way the game is currently played this is quite annoying

*•Health/ammo: This is simple, throw in a health and ammo block for the map editor. You take it and it respawns later.

*•Crouching: I personally would like to be able to crouch down, but I realize that this type of vision for a shooter may not be what the developers are trying to get out. I'd still suggest crouching as I don't see it 'slowing' down the game or having a significant negative impact.

*•Ladders: Fix these please. I'm sure people can vouch for falling off these too many times.

*•Free for all deathmatch spawning points: I realize people die fast, but I see multiple people spawning at the same area, or at least spawning on areas people are at. The limit on spawn locations seems to be pointless. I would suggest allowing more spawn locations to be placed (with a minimum of 8/8 and 16) and doing your best to place people at spawns as far away from people as possible.

*•Melee Weapons: I feel they have low distance or are not hitting. An larger indication of whether they hit or not would be very nice

*•Who's the enemy?: Half the time you can't tell the difference in critical situations between an ally or an enemy. Some form of indication like RED v BLUE would be nice even if it was an optional feature

*•Map Editing - Invisible boundaries: It would be nice to have a block that appeared invisible in game that you couldn't go through for boundaries and such. In the editor it could be sometime like a translucent red block with X on each side of it

I'll stop here and let other people say what they gotta say. I can't think of anything else at the moment.

title: A sort of gun comparsion guide

posts.h:
NOTE: This isn't the finished product

Anyways, since I haven't posted on these forums, I thought this would be a good way to kick-start my activity here.

THE SOMEWHAT COMPREHENSIVE BUT NOT REALLY GUIDE TO MOST WEAPONS IN BRICKFORCE


I'll start with a rundown on stats, as this section should be fairly short.

WHAT THE STATS MEAN

POW: POW, known better as Power states how much damage the weapon will do. A 100% power weapon such as the BWM will obviously do dramatically more damage than say, a 26% power weapon like the K1S.

RoF: RoF, known better as Rate of Fire states how fast the weapon will fire. The upside of a large RoF is that the gun will hail bullets. The downside is that if you don't control your fire by means such as burst firing, your shots will oftentimes land absolutely everywhere, since a high RoF so far is proportional to a low ACC.

ACC: ACC, better known as Accuracy states how far apart the bullets land from each other. This should seem fairly obvious, in the sense that you'll know that bullets from a gun with a higher ACC won't stray as far from it's intended destination as a gun with a low ACC. As mentioned previously, a gun with a high RoF often has a low ACC.

Recoil: I'm pretty sure recoil states how much your gun kicks upwards when you shoot a bullet. This factor probably works hand in hand with ACC to judge where your bullets will land. All sniper rifles have a 100% Recoil, although they only shoot 1 bullet at a time anyways.

Mobility: Mobility states how fast your character will move when you're holding the weapon. The higher the Mobility is, the faster you move.

Mag: Mag, better known as Magazine states how many bullets you'll have at your disposal. The less accurate weapons generally have more bullets to balance it out.

SNIPER RIFLES


Now, I'm pretty sure that all of them are capable of one shot kills, as I've used all of them save for the BSG69, because the stats on it were sub-par. Simple as that. The only real difference between them here is their recoil, magazine size and move speed. Sniper rifles are used for *shudder* trick shots, as well as picking people off and trolling them from long to mid distance. They can usually be avoided by bunnyhopping around randomly and burst firing at the wielders, unless there are more than 2 and they're competent, in which case you're dead unless you do some totally impossible to do thing like taking cover.

BSG69:

Power: 90
Rate of Fire: 4.5
Accuracy: 100
Recoil: 100
Mobility: 47.5
Mag: 60

From the stats, this gun looks relatively sub-par compared to it's cousins. I've never bothered to try it out, so I can't offer anything else.

Power: 100

Recoil: 100
Mobility: 47.5

This weapon has the exact same stats as every other sniper rifle except the BSG69. I think that really the only differences here are aesthetic and possibly scoping time, as this gun doesn't look nearly as cool as the other ones.

CS vets will probably remember this weapon as the AWP. I personally find it ever so slightly more accurate than the other ones for less orthodox shots such as jump shots.

Wait, so you're actually for something like the CoD and Battlefield 3 progression system than what we had when both series were initially released?

In bf1942, everyone had access to the exact same kits and there were little to no changes between the two opposing sides with exception to the original Japan vs America maps because the US forces initially had the no4 bolt-action rifle to use against the Japanese type 10 semi-auto rifle. When the GOTY and Anthology versions came out, they automatically had the proper version patches to have the properly coded weapon sets across all the maps. Even mods like the Desert Combat mod were balanced kit and vehicle wise.

Once Call of Duty was the same way as BF1942 except it was for a single player experience and as such had main competition in titles like Medal of Honor. Until it had "modern warfare" attached to its title, it was never about online multiplayer and everyone had access to the same weapons. Never before was there a console shooter where they attempted to pull a version of the Battlefield 2 progression system, but with a twist, choose to prestige to a higher level and do it all again. Personally I find such a system idiotic as it is just "Oh hey, I know you're happy to hit the level cap for this prestige level BUT you can get to a higher level on the next prestige tier, you just have to start from zero in all terms except for player tags!".

As stated earlier however, since this is a closed beta, they want to test out multiple things, which include:
1) Making sure weapons are somewhat balanced in some aspects and that there are no bugs when using them.
2) Making sure that weapon mastery levels are registered when attempting to purchase a weapon.
3) Making sure that some items such as character skins and some gear can only be obtained by specific purchasing options such as using brick points for treasure chest items, tokens for skins, and general points for maps.

Once Infernum decides to go to public Beta, all of the accounts will be wiped and balances set to null if not just enough for one new weapon or a map to be made instead of the current 100k for all three by default. Which would be your progression system I imagine.

title: Guide: How to tell the difference between a Hacker and Lag

posts.h:
Since it seems like Brick-Force appears to be the first online game a lot of the people around here have ever played and they're not familiar with the common phenomena of lag, I figured I'd do a community service and explain it for everyone.

First off, here's a great in depth explanation of lag, latency, ping, packet loss, etc.:
http://www.gamedev.net/page/resource...at-is-lag-r712

Here's a more basic breakdown:
Basically, when you move or shoot your weapon your computer sends that information over the interwebs to the server or host. The server has to collect this information from all the players. This information is called "packets". If you're really far from the server or your network connection is bogged down because you're downloading the latest Justin Bieber or Selena Gomez album (or whatever crap you kids listen to these days) then your packet will fall behind. Everyone else will be moving and shooting but you might not be able to tell and when you shoot where someone appears to be they may not actually be there.

Here are some common symptoms:
Players don't appear to be moving
Players don't appear affected by being hit or shot and may seem "invincible"
You can't move
Other players appear to be sliding, "teleporting" or moving extremely fast

You could experience one or possibly all of these symptoms intermittently or sporadically.

If you are experiencing lag you can:

If your internet connection sucks by design...deal with it.

Check your connection: www.speedtest.net (ignore the PC Tuneup/Start thing, just click on Begin the Test when it shows up) If speedtest shows you're not getting close to the advertised speed of your internet provider give them a call possibly, also try resetting or "cycling" your router. (Google it darnit)

Make sure you don't have a bunch of other programs running, sucking up bandwidth. If you have other computers on your network check them too if you have access to them.

Try joining a different game or advertise a game for players in a certain region, i.e. west coast, east coast.

Make sure you're using the proper client, i.e. U.S. / EU.

If you're the current room's game master, you can kick players taking a long time to load or connect. Hitting TAB in-game will show you a list of players along with their ping. Green is good. Yellow is so-so and Red is bad, m'kay. Now, if everyone other player on the player list is showing red, then it's likely that you might be the actual source of the problem.
posts.t: Guide: How to tell the difference between a Hacker and Lag

posts.h: Hi, you need to go to the "shop" menu and buy them with your points, then you must make sure you equip them.

title: Fast EXP Maps & The Rules Of Etiquette

posts.h:
It seems as though the fast,easy,quick, etc. EXP maps are growing in popularity, and really why wouldn't they? They are not pretty, they don't require any level of tactics, and they certainly don't help your Kills/Deaths ratio much. However, they do just what they advertise, allowing one to rack up thirty plus kills in minutes. I'm guessing some purists probably hate these maps, because even the greenest of nubes can level up fairly quickly using them.

So that being said, and even though they aren't much fun compared to stalking your prey in a big map, I have played in several of these easy exp maps. Yesterday I was playing one of the most carnage-creating maps of this type I have seen, with two pits on either side of a long, closed corridor. I was shocked when someone on the other team started to ask that I be kicked. I've never been kicked from a map and until yesterday no one I've played with wanted me kicked.

The complaint of the other player? I was being too aggressive. Now forgive me if I'm wrong, but the Fast EXP maps are all about Fast EXP, right? As soon as I spawn, it's time to put opposing players in my MG42S blender and press the whip button. I expect them to do the same to me, over and over, with no mercy and no strategy. The player who wasn't happy with me accused me of spawn killing, and so for a few minutes I tried to play nice in the sandbox and wait on my side until the opposition advanced. Not surprisingly, I ended up very, very dead.

So, what do you think? Are these maps good or bad? Should they be banned? And most curious to me, are there any rules in a Fast EXP death pit?

Spikekip
posts.t: Fast EXP Maps & The Rules Of Etiquette

posts.h:
The only 'FAST XP' maps I see consist of one side spawning in a box, And the other team spawning outside of the box, With access to all 4 gun placements.

I have a feeling it's not purists so much as balance people who hate these maps, Myself included. Maps without cover or 'arena' style maps I can deal with and even enjoy. But the typical 'FAST XP' maps need to be renamed something more accurate like 'FEESH IN A BARREL' because that's about all the skill those 'maps' (And I use that term VERY loosely) take.

Little more than TrollMaps designated to draw in unsuspecting fresh noob kills as the 'dominating' side is typically always the same color, And thus players who are in the know know which side to take. :P

FEESH IN A BARREL is a perfect way to describe them! The more I consider these maps, the less likely I am to play them. Though I don't care at all about my ratios (preferring to scare the **** out of players by running at them with a meat grinder of rounds), even the easy kills are no fun when you're just another "FEESH".

posts.h: The entire game!
I am looking forward to all my achievements, stats, tokens and points being reset...not. Darn it! I should start build some maps for first time.

Yeah, losing all the stats and points will not be fun, but I guess that's the nature of beta testing. I'm guessing that we won't have the huge amount of starting points/tokens either.

"and intriguing new items to be sold in the item shop for game currency or real money"

I hope these intriguing items for real money are not stat boosters. The model of f2p games which offer items for real money that can customise but not stat boost a players experience is to me the most fair across the board. There have been plenty of "f2p" games that I loved playing in beta which became pointless after launch because the buyable items created demi-gods. I hope that doesn't happen here . . .

That being said, I would have no problems spending some cash on sweet accessories, clothes, etc. on a game that I love, like Brick Force!
Looking forward to the Streamliner and jetpack for building. Trying to do a 'Giant Bedroom' map last night and had to put up 1x49x100 walls by myself. Block.By.Block XD

Giant Bedroom sounds AWESOME. I'm looking forward to the jet pack as well (though someone mentioned it might not be an automatic get). It really sux when you fall off super tall "scaffolding", not to mention having to erase it.

I was working on a giant castle, but thinking about the reset and the maps I've played, I have decided on some giant, animal sculpture related maps instead. Sounds crazy I know, but I've drawn it all out on graph paper . . . Oh man, I think I might be too into Brick Force

An external block editor could be useful as well in the future. Maps can be saved/loaded via a grid of colored cubes (I know more games do this save/load but the only one comes to mind is Voxatron.) in a .png complete with the snapshot. (The X, Y location of the pixel in the png represents the x, y position on the grid, The color indicates block type/height. )

title: How can I play Brick-Force in my browser?

posts.h:
In order to play Brick-Force in your browser, you first need the Unity Web Player.

The first time you try to log into the browser version, it will automatically redirect you to the download. Click on “Unity Web Player - Install Now” and save the installation file on your PC.

As soon as download is finished, double-click on the "UnityWebPlayer.exe" and follow through with the installation.
Then, start the Brick-Force browser version anew and reload the page.

You can now log into the game with your username and password.

Let's step back for a moment and look at the way things have been, and where they are right now. For all but the past day of this beta, we have had what really amounts to unlimited spending ability. Anything you wanted in the game could be had, and for good reason as the devs wanted everything tested. Everyone who has bothered to read has known about the impending changes, including loss of points/skills/rank.

Yesterday, we were all a bit shocked to log in after the server updates and find our gear and points stripped. It was also unsettling to see that we couldn't buy much of anything. That last point is one that I still believe we should have received a heads up on, and I understand the initial anger. I for one was making a few last minute changes to a huge map, excited to register it and receive feedback in the last week of closed beta; that's not happening now.

The devs are reading everything that is going on here, and they have clearly stated that there was a reason for doing what they did yesterday. Think of it as a user stress test; when everything is taken from your account and you only have enough points to buy a few things, what choices do you make? The devs are looking at the choices we make in the distribution of limited resources to pinpoint the aspects of the game that each player finds most important.

I have stated elsewhere how I feel about map creation, namely that it should be free; cut off the creativity and you kill the game. However, do you really think that any game developers would, after spending over a year in development and testing, shoot their creation in the heart right before launch by creating unrealistic limitations on every aspect of game play? I don't.

SpikeIP has the right idea. As to the points being placeholders, I can't find the topic he stated it in, But RedBrick mentioned that it is indeed temporary, And the devs did as well in the aforementioned sticky, Just not in so many words. (testing usually means 'for the duration of beta' unless otherwise stated as permanent!)

I also agree with Spike on the fact that a heads-up BEFORE such a major change would have saved some of the frustration, As well as a heads-up in the ingame notices of the changes. Mind, There's only so much text the in-game mail holds right now. Was expecting a reset near the next phase of the test to begin with, So I wasn't TOO shocked at the reset itself, So much as the lack of notice or detailed explanation.

Saying "We're working on it!" is fine, But a little more explanation would be good for those of us who aren't devs, Regular beta hoppers or otherwise 'in the know' about how these things work. :>

EDIT: Sorry if I came off the handle, But had to redirect several "OMG THIS SUCKS" threads to the sticky. Even then, People are stillg going to rage and I have to accept that, But even my patience and calmness has limits when surrounded by so much unfounded negativity. Glad it wasn't negative and sorry if I came off a bit sarcastic. Noobing it up all day will do that to you. XD
I'm glad there are players who understand what the devs are trying to do. Keep up the good work, we need more people to show the disappointed players everything isn't so bad!

It's not really hard to deal with a sniper, Except on maps where the sniper has cover and you're in a large open and low space. In any ranged fight, Right down to prehistory holding the higher ground has always meant one of three thigns for dealing with snipers:

(A) Coordinated fire on that spot from cover while some folk risk rushing the wall. Most good sniper spots are hard to aim at the base of.

In my own experiences with the Unity player, (Unless I'm wrong it's what the browser client is using!) it seems to run better on activeX-based browsers a bit better. (Internet exploder, Crum)
Even tho i just joined, i can say the client is as demanding as the browser version! It doesn't even lag on safari.

The browser version will require more of your connection ot the internet then the downloadable version. The unity player / browser funnels everything through your connection, graphics, sound, saved information, etc etc. The downloadable version spreads some of the work to your computer and its components, your graphics, whether onboard or external, handle the bulk of what you are seeing graphically, your sound card processes most of the sound on its own, some info is saved on your hard drive, etc etc.
There are good and bad to both, browser based being a connection hog, and client based being a bit more of a hardware hog. If you have a crap machine and a good connection speed, the browser game will be your best bet. If you have a decent rig and a decent connection the client version is your best bet.

Wizard's Guide To Brick-Force Monopolization
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section 1- Basic tips for beginners
Section 2- Extra help for more advenced players
Section 3- Hints and Tips on Guns, Maps and Tastics
Section 4- Map Creation
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-{Section One}-

Beginning- The 1st time you play DO NOT BUY ANYTHING. Use the basic Submachine Gun that they give you for free.
Play a few games and get a basic understanding of the game pysics.

{TIP}- the Basic submachine gun is good for short-mid range killing. Long range is possible but the chances of getting spoted is very high. During close or mid range combat spam is recommended.

The best way to avoid death is to do a little shooting here and there, NEVER stay at the same spot after 2+ kills.
Try to keep your death as less as possible for it will effect the amount you earn per game.

{TIP}- If you want to buy a different gun, I suggest one of the guns that are on sell and only buy the 1day guns.

The reason for 1day is because of the Shop prices being outrageous. Besides that using the same thing over and over gets old very fast.

When firing your gun spraying is NOT the best idea, with the exception of the submachine gun, all the others have a wild recoil. It is best if you "tap fire" aka clicking your mouse in a constant rate. This will help lower the recoil and help your aim and hit rate.

In every game try to keep your Kill more or equal to your death. Each game should give you the minimum of around 200 points per game.

{TIP}- Do Not waste your points on things like cloths, pants, shoes and other trash at the moment. They do nothing for you at this point when your trying so hard to save some points.

{TIP}- If you have bought a gun from the shop make sure you earn more then the gun cost, if not you are losing money.

Go on and get some more points, hide behide what ever you can find that can save you, use some tastic and out think your enemies. Until you get over 10k of points, thats when the mass point is coming in. (go on to section 2)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-{Section 2}-

If you are here you are, 1 very good or 2 got pass Section 1. (if not go back)

When you reach this point thats when you can start farming points to get all the crap you ever wished for.

If you have over 10k of points, go buy a Character Head/Mask thing. They will give you 10 luck, 10 extra points and 10 something else that I forgot. Again only buy the 1day at this point.

This will help you when earning points, of course it is not a must have it is just a boost to your gain.

{TIP}- DO NOT BUY stat gaining items unless you are sure you will be playing a lot that day. EX. sat/sun/holidays

Now that you are ready to take on the world, go down to section 3 for all the tips and hints about maps, guns and tastics.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(rest is in a replay since posts are limited to 5000 words lol)

-{Section 3}-

[MAPS & GUN USAGE]
There are tons of maps out there since we can make our own. But to have the best outcome you need a map that suits your playing style.

Sinpers- When using a sniper it is best to avoid direction fire, meaning a large map and large amounts pf hiding places are the best.

{TIP}- DO NOT TRY no scoping. It will not work, if you are traped in directed fire, 1 find some sort of cover, 2 take out your pistol and get ready to rush the enemy.

Assault Rifle- These are made for short-mid and somewhat long range battle. The thing is most of these ARs slow you down. So a map with decent amount of cover and places to ambush is the way to go. Avoid large maps they will murder you.

{TIP}- It is best to tap fire or the recoil might get the best of you.

Submachine Gun- They are mostly made for close to mid range combat. Long range is not the best since the hit rate will drop dramatically. These are like the ARs but its more of a "spam you in the face till you die thing".
Since it should be in close range, the extra speed of a SMG should take out most people. For this gun a small map is better. Smaller the map better chances of someone running into you so you can pump them full of lead.
Ambush is the best choice with this fast firing hunk of metal.

{TIP}- Try to calculate the amount of shoots needed to kill a enemy. With the fast fire rate comes with the problem of running out of ammo.

Heavy Machinegun- With this thing you move like a snail, not the best acc also the recoil wild. But the damage is (if i remember correctly) the highest besides the sniper rifles. Since this gun have a wild recoil it is best for small maps and for charging. It have more ammo in a round so it is made for clearing a group in a small area. Mid ranges are ok but not the best choice. Long range with this is like using a blow dart to shoot the moon.

{TIP}- Try to tap fire and control the recoil as much as possible. When moving switch to the pistol for faster movement and better chance of getting to cover.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------{Section 4}-

[MAP CREATION]
This is the only FPS that I know that let you make you own maps. By making maps others can rate your map and you get something known as "Brick Points" so far they are nearly usless but who knows, maybe later they will be very helpful. So get going and make a map!

In order to rack up more votes for you map you must consider the following.

1. Is the map fair? One sided maps will only get low rating or no ratings at all. So making both sides equal is a good idea.

2. Is the structures or hiding spots usful? Each place that is used as cover should have 1 way to over come. This will prevent players camping in one place and just destorying the other team.

3. Is the map beginner friendly? For people who have just started to play and is thrown into a twisted maze like place is not fun. The others that have played more have the uperhand since they understand where is where. It is best to make simple maps that doesnt twist your noodles into a pretzel.

Brick-Point Use?
The only thing you can do with it is use it in a lottery to hopfully get some special guns. But its not worth it, norm guns are just as good and easyer to come by. Save them for later, they should have some sort of plan for them.

Extra Sugestions-

Be nice to other and dont talk trash. People like friendly people that dont rage on others.

Dont say you must rate the map a 10. Just tell them to rate if you like and thank them afterwards.

Dont be a jerk and rage kick people just because they are better then you. You learn from losing so you should be thanking them.

Have fun. Its very simple, if you who made the map hates it and/or feels its too hard, then it probably is.
Take suggestions from others and see if you can improve your map.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Thankyou to everyone!

title: Easiest way to get Brick points?

posts.h:
Einen guten Tag liebe/r Brick-Force Spieler/in & der Rest der Community!

Soo.. unser Konzept ist nun beinahe fertig. Alles was uns fehlt ist die Freischaltung unserer Domain! Achja, unser Projekt wird in Kürze in die "BETA" gehen und wir freuen uns natürlich über so viele Tester wie nur möglich!

Es wird mehrere "tolle" Dinge auf einmal geben. Zum einem der versprochene Cup (das Turnier), welcher wahrscheinlich einmal im Monat oder einmal die Woche stattfinden wird. Dieser sogenannte Brick-Cup wird in zwei Strukturen aufgeteilt, einmal der Hardcore-Cup und der Fun-Cup!
Zum anderen haben wir noch unser System, in welchem ihr auf der Seite registrierte Clans herausfordern könnt. Wer die ESL kennt, weiß wie das alles abläuft!

Fun-Cup
Der Fun-Cup wird jede Woche stattfinden. Anmeldefrist ist 1 Tag vor dem Beginn. Es ist nur möglich sich als Team anzumelden. Ab diesem Zeitpunkt wird unser System die Teams zufällig in die Gruppen einordnen. Bei diesem Cup geht es nicht ums gewinnen, sondern er dient ausschließlich dem Vergnügen. In dem Cup können keine Punkte o.ä. errungen werden, somit wird man auch in keiner Platzierung vorzufinden sein.

Hardcore-Cup
Dieser Cup wird 3 Wochen im Voraus angekündigt werden, damit alle Teams genug Zeit haben sich aufzustellen und anzumelden. 5 Tage vor Beginn wird die Anmeldefrist auslaufen. Ab diesem Zeitpunkt wird unser System die Teams zufällig in die Gruppen einordnen. Es gibt keine Zuordnung aufgrund des Rankings. Für jeden Sieg bekommt man eine gewisse Anzahl an Punkten, im Finale mehr zum Beispiel im Viertelfinale. Für die gewonnenen Punkte kann man sich später viele tolle Features kaufen! Der Sieger des Turniers bekommt einen Preis und eine Auszeichnung des Ranking-Systems.

System der Cups
Der Fun(Hardcore)-Cup ist als KO System aufgebaut. Es gibt keine Gruppenphase. Der Sieger des ersten Spieles, spielt gegen den Sieger des zweiten Spieles, etc.

Zeitlich läuft der Fun(Hardcore)-Cup wie folgt ab
Jeder Finalabschnitt dauert insgesamt 2 Tage. Als Finalabschnitt bezeichne ich das Halbfinale, 1/4-Finale, etc. In diesem Zeitraum können die Teams, welche gegeneinander kämpfen müssen, den Zeitpunkt ihres Matches selbst entscheiden. Dadurch sollen Probleme bei der zeitlichen Austragung des Matches vermieden werden. Nachdem 2 Tage vorüber sind, beginnt der nächste Finalabschnitt. Falls ein Match nicht stattfindet, wird ausgelost werden, welches von den beiden Teams in die nächste Runde kommt. Wenn das Finale innerhalb der 2 Tage nicht zustande kommt, wird um weitere 2 Tage verlängert. Nach diesen 2 Tagen wird das Finale als ungültig erklärt und es gibt keine Sieger.

Im Falle eines Unentschiedens zwischen 2 Teams, wird das Match solange wiederholt bis ein Sieger gefunden wurde.

Teams
Die Teams, die sich für einen Cup angemeldet haben, dürfen ihre Aufstellung nicht verändern. Es dürfen keine Mitglieder des Teams während des Turniers ausgetauscht werden.

Spielmodus
Der für einen Cup am besten geeignete Spielmodus ist der Defusion-Modus. Für alle, die nicht wissen, was der Modus beinhaltet, hier noch einmal die Definition von der Brick-Force Website: ,,Ziel des roten Teams ist es, eine Bombe zu platzieren, Ziel des blauen Teams ist es, diese Bombe zu entschärfen. Jedes Mitglied von Team rot trägt je eine Bombe (zusätzlich zu deren Waffen natürlich), die an einem der zwei Defusion-Spots angebracht werden muss, die jede Defusion-Karte enthält. Platziert bzw. entschärft die Bombe, indem ihr die Action-Taste „E“ gedrückt haltet. Das wird eine Weile dauern, also bringt euch Beschützer mit! Sobald eine Bombe am Sprengziel platziert wurde, wird ein Countdown beginnen, der jedem auf der Karte angezeigt wird. Wenn die Zeit abgelaufen ist, geht die Bombe hoch, und Team blau verliert. Wenn die Bombe nicht in der vorgegebenen Zeit hochgeht, wird Team rot verlieren. Ihr könnt beide Sprengziele jederzeit auf eurem Radar erkennen.“

Die Anzahl der zu erreichenden Siege liegt bei 9 pro Spielhälfte.

Kontrolle
Um zu Kontrollieren wie die Matches ausgegangen sind müssen wir noch eine Software entwickeln die der, der ESL ähnelt (Für unwissende: Eine Software die alle paar Sekunden Bilder macht, hilft auch gegen Cheater), das Endergebnis muss dann nur noch von jedem beteiligten Team gescreent werden und dann in unser System geladen werden. Der Rest wird von unserem Team geregelt.
Die neuen Match-Paare werden dann wieder vom System erstellt und können in einem Extra Reiter auf der Seite nachgeschaut werden ebenso wie die Ergebnisse.

Was zur Zeit gesucht/benötigt wird

-Homepage/Forum/Webspace
-Jemand mit guten HTML-Kenntnissen
-Jemand der sich ein wenig mit Grafiken auskennt
-Ein oder zwei Leute die das Konzept mit mir verfeinern
Mit freundlichen Grüßen,
xMirko97 [Konzept] (& GS-Sponsoring [Website etc.] Ellcrys [Text])

Dear Brick-Force friends,

I must admit that I am a little addicted to playing Brick-Force Death-Match. Even if it is a little quirky (like getting kicked off-line or the lag issues)... there is still plenty of action where everyone can run around and have fun... I love it.

I can also say that I have grown to enjoy helping the newbies who are just starting with things such as the following:

1. I enjoy answering their questions like “What are brick points for?”
2. I enjoy giving a few helpful hints and ideas also.
3. I also enjoy helping the newbies have fun by starting a Death-Match for them to run around in.

I even like it when my character dies almost instantly after re-spawning (LOL). Everybody gets to have fun by running around and shooting at everything.

I wish I could get paid to do this because I love it.

You have a great game, a great environment, and great people... and a great price, which is free.

In my opinion it's got just as much action as the big name expensive games, and it's a lot better than the cheap flash games that are out there.

I even love the help in the forums from others gamers, and the admins.

Thanks... I appreciate all you folks. 8D

Yours Truly,

Crazy-Lenny
U.S.

Name: Bear
Brick-Force Username: Gravebear
Age: 32

Tell us a bit about yourself.
I am a father of three and I spend most of my time working or with my kids. I am a programmer for a living working at CnC Robotics and have enjoyed computers all my life. I spent many years as a musician in a touring death metal band and currently fill in as a studio bassist/guitarist/drummer to help with production of a band’s music. I spent time working as a tester for another well-known game and worked directly with one of the programmers to test new ideas. I started gaming back during the Atari days and have since tried to keep up to date. I also used to run a construction company for almost nine years and worked on new homes and commercial buildings as a painter and drywaller. I have to say that experience really helps me in Build mode. My kids many may know as Armydog and Dspair also play Brick-Force with me and we enjoy our family bonding time building and shooting. My family and I have made Brick-Force not just a game but a way to enjoy family time together

How long have you been playing Brick-Force?
Since the final week of closed beta.

How did you discover Brick-Force?
I am always reading reviews on new games and products releasing. I read about Brick-Force on MMOHut and decided to try it out.

What do you like most about Brick-Force?
The community! I feel players develop a greater sense of friendship that allows you to do more than just shoot each other in-game. Most of the friends I have made are from building, others are from clans. I find players are very helpful and always willing to have fun.

What other games do you play?
Currently just Brick-Force, however there aren’t too many games that I have not played.

Do you rock out to any music while playing Brick-Force?
Yes, I love music! I mainly like metal, however I listen to all types of music.

When you’re not playing Brick-Force, what else are you up to?
Usually when I am not playing I am busy with my kids playing ball, swimming, or watching movies.

Build mode or Shooter mode, take your pick.
This is like picking which of my kids is my favorite: I can’t! I could never like one more than the other because I would hate to think of the game without either.

What is your most memorable experience in the game?
When I recorded my map review for a map I crated, Outpost 66.

Is there a story behind your username?
My animal spirit is the Bear. I am 75% Native American and I am proud of my heritage. Grave was added after realizing that I am getting old.

Spider-Man or Batman?
Batman. Batmobile, enough said.

Email newsletters often accidentally end up in the spam folder in your email, even though you signed up for them! To avoid this, you will have to “whitelist” the sender, but this is slightly different for each different email program and service.
In this post, I will show you how to stop your newsletters from being treated like “spam” or “junk” and make sure they end up in your inbox for Gmail, Yahoo! Mail, Microsoft Outlook AOL, Hotmail, Mozilla Thunderbird and many other email clients and webmail services.

What Is Whitelisting?

It tells your email program (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail and AOL) that emails from news@news.brick-force.com aren’t spam. To do this you need to add the newsletter sender’s email address to a “whitelist”.
The method varies slightly depending on which email provider or program you use.
If your email service/program is not listed here, these instructions will probably give you enough information to work it out so try and have a go anyway. If you want to provide a guide on how to whitelist emails on your email provider, please send your guide to our support team as a suggestion: http://support.infernum.com
Our staff will then forward all details to the Community Team.

Whitelist Emails in your Spam/Junk Mail Folder if you do not want them there

If you find an email in your spam folder that is not spam always take a moment to mark it as “not spam” or “not junk”. With this, your email program automatically adds the sender to the whitelist.

How To Whitelist Our Newsletter

Find your email service or email client and click the link get to the instructions below. You need to whitelist the following email address.

Attention
We have tried to deliver detailed explanations, however, not all buttons and provider links could be verified for all offered languages. Please check your email account directly for correct button and link names.
Newsletter subscribers: news@news.brick-force.com

Email Provider List

GMail:

  1. First, if you find email from the news@news.brick-force.com in your Gmail spam folder, select our email and click the “Not Spam” button
  2. Next, open an email that you have received from us
  3. Click on the little arrow next to the reply button:
  4. Click “Add news@news.brick-force.com to Contacts list”

Hotmail:
You must add news@news.brick-force.com to your “Safe List” as follows:

  1. First, if you find email from news@news.brick-force.com in your Hotmail junk folder, open the email and click “Not Junk”
  2. Next, check to see if news@news.brick-force.com appears in the “Blocked Senders” list. You can access this list by clicking on the link at the bottom of the junk mail page. If necessary, select the Brick-Force email and click on the “Remove” button.
  3. Next, open your mailbox and click “Options” in the upper right hand corner
  4. At the top of the page, click on the “Preventing junk email” link
  5. Next, click on “Safe senders”
  6. Copy and paste news@news.brick-force.com where it says “sender or domain to mark as safe”
  7. Click the “Add to list” button

Yahoo! Mail:
You must set up a “filter”, but first:

  1. If you find email from news@news.brick-force.com in your “Yahoo! Spam” folder, open the email and click “No Spam”
  2. If you find emails from news@news.brick-force.com in your “Blocked Addresses” list, select the email and click “Remove Block”
  3. To see this list, click on Options and then Spam.
Now to create the filter:

  1. Open Yahoo! Mail and click on “Mail Options” in the upper right hand corner.
  2. Select “Filters” (in the bottom left corner)
  3. On the Filters page, click “Add”
  4. Select the “From header:” rule, and add “contains” and news@news.brick-force.com to match all mail from Brick-Force.com.
  5. Click the “Choose Folder” pull down menu and select ‘Inbox’
  6. Pick the Add Filter button

Comcast Email:

  1. Sign into Webmail.
  2. On the left navigation menu, click Address Book.
  3. Click Add Contact.
  4. Under the General tab, in the box under the Email Address, enter newsletter@brick-force.com
  5. Click the Add button.
  6. If you have enabled “Restrict Incoming Email,” also do the following:
  7. Select Preferences.
  8. Select “Restrict Incoming Email”. If Enable Email Controls is set to Yes, then you are restricting incoming emails.
  9. Select Allow email from addresses listed below.
  10. Enter newsletter@brick-force.com
  11. Click the Add button.

Verizon.net Email:

  1. Go to your account and click on the Address Book link in the left column.
  2. Select Create Contact.
  3. The Add Address Book Entry screen appears. In the Email field, enter newsletter@ brick-force.com
  4. In the Nickname field, type brick-force.com
  5. Select Save.

AOL.com Webmail:
You must add news@news.brick-force.com to your AOL address book as follows:

  1. Search for email from us in the Spam folder. If you find an email in the Spam folder, then open it and click the “Not Spam” button.
  2. Click the Contacts link (or open your AOL Address Book)
  3. Click the +New button.
  4. In the New Contact window, type news@news.brick-force.com into the ‘Primary E-Mail 1’ field
  5. Click “Create”

Email Client List

AOL Email Client:
New Subscribers: add the “From” address to your AOL address book:

  1. Click the Mail menu and select Address Book.
  2. Wait for the “Address Book” window to pop up, then click the Add button.
  3. Wait for the “Address Card for New Contact” window to load.
  4. Once loaded, cut and paste the “From” email address into the “Other E-Mail” field.
  5. Make our From address the “Primary E-Mail” address by checking the corresponding checkbox.
  6. Click the Save button.
Existing Subscribers: If you are already a subscriber but the email isn’t getting through, the email may be in your AOL Spam Folder. Open web mail and look in your Spam Folder. If your find our email in your spam folder open it and click the “This Is Not Spam” button. Then add the “From address” onto your Address Book as outlined in the “New Subscribers” instructions above.

Microsoft Outlook:

  1. On the Tools menu, click Options
  2. On the Preferences tab, click Junk E-mail
  3. On the Safe Senders tab, click Add
  4. Add news@news.brick-force.com where it says “Add address”.
  5. Click OK

Mozilla Thunderbird:
You need to add us to your address book, and set the Junk Mail Controls to whitelist your address book.

  1. First, check your Junk folder. If you find email from brick-force.com, right-click on our email and choose “Mark as Not Junk”
  2. Next, click the “Address Book” button
  3. Highlight the Personal Address Book (left column)
  4. Click on “New Contact”
  5. In the “Contact” tab, set “Email” to newsletter@brick-force.com
  6. Click “Ok” and close the Address Book
  7. From the main Thunderbird menu, choose “Tools > Account Settings”
  8. For each email account, expand the settings and choose “Junk Settings” from the expanded account settings.
  9. Ensure “Personal Address Book” is checked under “Do not mark mail as junk if the sender is in:”
  10. Once you have done this for each email account, click OK

BlackBerry:

  1. Scroll up to a message from brick-force.com
  2. Get to the field where this name is listed, click the Berry button and then click Show Address.
  3. Select and copy the email address to the clipboard.
  4. Go into Address Book and find the user.
  5. Select Save.
  6. Click to edit it, and then click the Berry button to add another email address.
  7. Paste it in and click Save

Apple Mail / OSX:

  1. First, if email from news@news.brick-force.com ends up in your junk folder, highlight or open it and click “Not Junk” at the top of your screen.
  2. Go to “Mail” > “Preferences”
  3. Go to “Mail” > “Preferences” Go to the Rules tab
  4. Select Add Rule
  5. Give this rule a name such as “Email from brick-force.com”
  6. Create a rule that says “If any of the following conditions are met: ‘From’ ‘Contains’” and then paste in “brick-force.com”
  7. From the actions, select ‘Move message’ to mailbox ‘Inbox’.
  8. Click “OK”

I wouldn't compare Minecraft to Brick-Force because they're 2 different fields of gaming. Brick-Force is a PvP, battle oriented game, while Minecraft is a PvE, sand-box game.

They both have their advantages and disadvantages.
-Minecraft's advantages are that: it's appealing to the creative gamer, has 'realistic' worlds and physics, can be played offline, has essentially "limitless" worlds, high-quality game play, and a devoted development team. With Mojang backing Minecraft, I don't see it disappearing for a while.
-Disadvantages are: ...

-Brick-Forces advantages are: it's appealing to the PvP/1st-Person Shooter gamer, has comfortably community oriented UI (including lobbies, public chat channels, friend list system, etc), community creations are easily available for public use (maps and stuff), and users can open public or password-protected private playing rooms hosted by commercial-grade servers.
-Disadvantages are: It's another Unity-based game (always means use of Unity default prefabs which is a perfect recipe for frame rate "lag"), it has it's fair share of bugs (that's Unity for you), physics are messy (again Unity), server bandwidth is 'low', and it's almost entirely Free-to-Play (opens the game to the potentially worst of the worst trolls, hackers/cheaters, and foul mouth'd children the internet has ever seen).

I personally feel that Brick-Force would have been better off being built in the Source Engine, and available for purchase or download on the "Steam" Client. Plenty of games have been built in the Source Engine with the look Brick-Force was going for, except successfully of course. The default Unity 'Toon shading' prefab is never a suitable shader for any professional IP's.

Do you love building, sharing and playing? Join the Brick-Brigade today!

The Brick Brigade was established with goal of rewarding players who want to share their Brick-Force experience, build the coolest maps and develop the community. The Brick Brigade celebrates everything that is great about Brick-Force and its players.

What's required of you to join the Brick Brigade? Nothing you don't already do, that's the beauty of it! Whether you're a Brick-Force Youtuber, streamer or wiki contributor, we have special forum avatars for you.

Visit the Brick Brigade page to see the full list of avatars and requirements needed to earn your title. Once you've fulfilled the requirements necessary for a title, email community@brick-force.com with evidence and we will award you with the avatar.

Serve your game proudly, soldiers.

This is the submissions thread for the "Design a Weapon" launch competition.

The Bomber Bees are up to no good and have stolen all of Cooper’s weapons! You are tasked with creating a new weapon for him to defend Brick-World against the Bees.

This is your chance to design and name a weapon in Brick-Force!

Guns, melee, grenades – any category is welcome. You imagine it, send it to us, and if we choose your weapon, who knows, it could end up in the game!

Guidelines

  • The weapon design must fit into the Brick-Force universe. As much as we love super-powered laser beams shot out of eyeballs, that’d just be silly in the game.

  • Your design should also be an original creation, so no photos of existing weapons!

  • The top ten designs will be chosen by Infernum Productions and EXE Games. On August 3, 2012, players will be able to vote for the weapon they would like to see in-game.

  • Submissions must be sent in JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF or PNG format.

We look forward to seeing all of the cool ideas you come up with!

Submit your designs below!

When I first read about this contest I was excited and began thinking of original yet simple weapons that would fit in with the Brick-Force universe. I was sure I could come up with something unique, and my imagination came up with some cool idea, some random ideas, and some strange ideas which I began to filter through. I finally settled on the idea of a Chemical or Electrical mine that a player could simply place and forget. I've posted a video and two JPEG images at the bottom of this thread, with the video offering a simple explanation of how the item would work while the next few text segments will explain how the items would work with more detail.

BF-2012 Chemical Mine:

The BF-2012 Chemical Mine is an item a player would bury in the ground, releasing a pinkish cloud similar to the BKGSS440 Smoke Grenade ( already found in the game ) that would cause minor chemical burns ( Sorry folks, no flame effects ) to the player triggering it as well as people who walk through the cloud. The chemicals would stay in the air for same amount of time as the smoke from the BKGSS440 Smoke Grenade and damage the player for 10-15 seconds every 2-3 second, doing ( over time ) a total of 25 damage to a player's health points while doing 50 damage to a player's armor. A player using the mine would spawn with 1 mine, and the mine would be removed from play upon the player's death meaning the player would need to plant a mine after he respawned.

BF-2012 Electrical Mine:

The BF-2012 Electrical Mine is an item a player would bury in the ground. They either would produce a small electrical shock ( which other players could not see ) doing an instant 25 damage to hit points only/causing temporary blindness like the Flashbang or acting like a stationary Flashbang doing no damage but being able to blind an enemy up to five times like the Flashbang. Of the two options for the electrical mine I would have to say the second ( causing a Flashbang effect up to five times while doing no damage ) is my preferred choice of the two. The item would be triggered when stepped on.

The video was taken at my mother's house with the images taken from the video and placed as JPEG into this forum. I hope that everybody enjoys seeing my hard work even if it is not an item they desire to see in game. My thanks to the Brick-Force community for the inspiration. I look forward to seeing more entries and hope play some fun matches with you all in-game!



Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3P7X1z3u1bs
